title: Does credit flowing back make labs share? 27 problems, labs choose: traditional, α 1, α 0.2 × 5 runs, $0.40 a lab (Nov 22)
question: When labs choose what to publish and when, does credit flowing back make them share more, and does the community prove more? [B]
answer: No clear difference. Labs published 92% of their lemmas at once at α 1 and 96% at α 0.2 (+4 points, range −3 to +12): they share almost everything either way. Targets proved were about the same (about 20 to 21 of 27). Lead: at α 0.2 labs built more on each other's work.

results.heading: Labs choose on the bigger set, knowledge reward off (2026-11-22 to 23)
results.html:
Result. Setups: traditional (public when a target is proved, α 1, m 0, m_bit 0, f 0); the lab chooses when to publish with α 1 or α 0.2 (m 0, m_bit 0, f 0). 4 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash labs, $0.40 a lab ($1.60 a run), labs cannot stop early, 5 runs per setup, 15 in all, about $24 at the fixed reference price. 27 targets, depth 1 to 7. Streamed live on oso.network.

Measure fixed in advance: the share of lemmas published at once, α 0.2 against α 1. Result: 92% (95% range 85% to 98%) at α 1, 96% (93% to 99%) at α 0.2; difference +4 points (−3 to +12). No clear difference: labs shared nearly everything at both α.

Targets proved, of 27 (mean, 95% range over 5 runs): traditional 20.0 (18.5 to 21.5), α 1 20.6 (19.5 to 21.7), α 0.2 21.2 (20.6 to 21.8). α 0.2 minus traditional +1.2 (−0.3 to +2.7); α 0.2 minus α 1 +0.6 (−0.5 to +1.7). Every run stalled at 20 to 21 targets; the deepest ones (X1, X6) were tried and failed to the end of the money.

Looked at after the results (leads only): results that built on another lab's work: 6.4 a run (traditional), 11.4 (α 1), 16.0 (α 0.2). Lemmas proved: 14.6, 14.0, 23.0. Targets proved again by a second lab: 11.0, 12.6, 19.2, so more building on others came with more repeated target work too.
